permutation_test.null_hypothesis: treatment labels are exchangeable across rows given the pooled frame

interpretation_limits: Diagnostic on a pooled frame. Campaign and customer identifiers are absent, so campaign-level variation in treatment rates, post-randomization preselection, a non-pre-treatment covariate and non-uniform assignment are not distinguishable here.
The permutation null assumes exchangeable rows. Repeated customers would break it, and the file does not let that be checked.
An estimated propensity strictly inside (0, 1) does not demonstrate positivity or ignorability; it is a fitted value, not a design probability.
Rejecting the pooled-IID null does not certify any particular alternative, and does not show the dataset paper's per-campaign randomization was wrong.

reweighting.note: Reweighting by the estimated propensity leaves an effective sample size of 4 out of 8,743. A handful of extreme weights would carry the whole estimate, so estimating e(X) is not a repair for the identification problem here; it relocates it into the variance.

verdict.decision: Keep the dataset as a conditional benchmark. Do not promote a causal claim from a constant propensity; report IPW and DR results as sensitivity analyses under stated identification assumptions.
verdict.headline: out-of-fold treatment ROC-AUC 0.6355, permutation p = 0.009901
